data_quality_notes:
RESEARCH WAS NOT TRUNCATED. The research phase ran 06:01-06:37 ET and finished inside budget, closing with a RESEARCH COMPLETE block at 06:57 and a FINAL STATE block at 07:04. candidates.jsonl held 18 lines resolving to 12 distinct positions, and all 12 are published. Nothing was reconstructed from prose.

WHAT THIS REPORT MOSTLY IS. Eleven of the twelve rows are position management on an existing book, not new risk: five CLOSE instructions (CCJ, SNX, and the long_term longs in NKE, LULU and LCII), two shorts held to be trimmed at their targets (NKE, LULU), and four amendments (DAL cut to half size into tomorrow's print, CEG hold and never add, DINO and EEM each trimmed by half). Only PEP is a genuinely new idea. Acted on in full, the book goes from 16 open positions to 10 — five closed by instruction plus GDX, which closed itself when the 2026-10-07 low of 84.36 went through its 85.40 stop.

TWO ROWS EACH FOR NKE AND LULU, AND THIS IS NOT A DUPLICATE. Each symbol carries two separate open positions pointing opposite ways: a long_term LONG being closed and a swing SHORT being held. Deduplication was done on (symbol, direction), not on symbol, which is the same key merge_report uses for one live position per side. Dropping the buy rows would leave two stop-less losing longs open with no instruction; dropping the sell rows would abandon the two positions actually making money.

SIX INSTRUCTIONS WERE MIRRORED INTO THE WATCHLIST BEFORE ENFORCEMENT, ON PURPOSE. validate_report.py --enforce rebuilds a demoted row's watchlist entry from scratch and does not copy catalyst.action, so a demoted row loses its instruction and the reader is told to 'republish once the numbers check out' about a position they are being told to close today. Four closes cannot be made to pass and the reason is structural rather than sloppy: a position being retired at a loss has its entry above the market and its honest downside below it, so the ratio describes a trade nobody would now enter. SNX fails at 1.40:1 against the 2.0 swing floor once the stop is widened to an honest 234.00; NKE long 1.44:1, LULU long 1.67:1 and LCII 1.69:1 against the 2.5 long_term floor at bear cases of 26.00, 76.00 and 68.00. CEG is mirrored for the same reason on a different check — its 250.00 stop sits 1.67 ATR below the 272.00 entry against a 2.0 ATR floor, and widening it to 245.70 would cut the ratio to 1.82:1, so it fails either way while still being a live +10.1% position that must carry a do-not-add instruction. None of these six were demoted on doubt about the decision; raising a target or shrinking a bear case to clear a floor is exactly the gaming config/strategy.md forbids, so the arithmetic was left honest and the instruction was moved somewhere it survives. CCJ was deliberately re-captured at its original levels so that it passes and its CLOSE action reaches the reader directly. DAL is the sixth, mirrored on a pre-market spread artifact rather than on anything structural — see the spread note below.

ONE SOURCE URL WAS REPOINTED, AND IT WOULD OTHERWISE HAVE WIPED THE REPORT. Research cited the raw Nasdaq API path it calls through market_data.py — api.nasdaq.com/api/quote/<SYM>/historical — for the price history behind every idea. A plain HEAD on that path returns 404 even with the query parameters attached, because it is an API endpoint rather than a page, so check_sources correctly read it as a dead link and ALL TWELVE ideas hard-failed on it. Left alone, --enforce would have demoted every recommendation and published a report with none. Each of those URLs has been repointed at Nasdaq's public historical page for the same symbol, which is the human-readable view of exactly the data that was fetched, and all ten replacements were HEAD-checked to 200 during synthesis. No underlying claim changed and no source was invented. The remaining unverifiable citations are honest: the finnhub API endpoints return 401 without a key and FRED times out on HEAD, both of which the validator treats as unverified rather than wrong.

THREE SPREAD FAILURES ARE PRE-MARKET QUOTE ARTIFACTS, NOT TRADEABLE SPREADS, AND THEY WERE NOT EDITED AWAY. Validation at 06:47 ET reads DAL at bid 79.53 / ask 84.32 (5.85%), SNX at 228.60 / 290.00 (23.68%) and LCII at 76.00 / 127.39 (50.53%). Those are indicative pre-open quotes on names that trade roughly $573M, $256M and $27.5M a day respectively; a mega-cap airline does not have a 5.85% spread, and none of these will survive the opening auction. The check has no market-session guard, so it fires anyway and will demote DAL on an artifact — which is why DAL's half-size instruction is mirrored into the watchlist alongside the five structural ones. Nothing was done about the numbers themselves: a bid/ask is not synthesis's to adjust, and inventing a tighter one to clear a check is the exact failure the validation layer exists to catch. SNX and LCII are being closed regardless, so for them the flag changes nothing. The practical instruction it does justify: use limit orders pre-open, never market.

RATIO CLUSTERING — FLAGGED, WITH THE MITIGATION. Six swing ratios land between 2.07 and 2.42 against a 2.0 floor (LULU short 2.07, DINO 2.10, CEG 2.18, EEM 2.27, DAL 2.35, NKE short 2.42), which is the signature of targets fitted to clear the bar. The mitigating fact, which should be weighed rather than assumed away: every one of those six is a pre-existing open position whose levels were set at publication between 2026-08-21 and 2026-10-05 and are unchanged today, so the clustering reflects the floor having filtered at original publication rather than anything fitted this morning. No target was moved to make a ratio work. The genuinely open question is whether the floor was being gamed on those earlier days.

STOPS WERE CHECKED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, AND THE FORWARD LENS MATTERS HERE. ATR14 was refetched this run for all ten symbols and every value matched the research log. Measured from entry, every published swing stop clears its asset-class ATR floor except CEG (1.67 ATR against 2.0). But nobody has moved these stops since the positions were opened, so measured from today's price several winners now risk more than they stand to make: CEG 0.41:1 forward, NKE short 0.34:1, DINO 0.69:1, LULU short 0.74:1, SNX 0.86:1, EEM 0.95:1. That is the reason four rows say trim or halve rather than hold, and why no row anywhere in this report says add. A structural note for whoever maintains this: there is no way to express a trailed stop in this schema without failing check_stop_distance, because raising a stop toward a filled entry drives |entry-stop|/ATR toward zero — which is why every one of these positions still carries its original stop. CCJ is the warning against using the forward lens alone: it shows the best forward ratio on the book at 6.99:1 purely because its 135.00 target sits 11.83 ATR away and is not a real target. Forward R:R flatters any idea with a fantasy target; it is a trim signal, never an entry signal.

CONVICTION: FOUR ROWS ARE DELIBERATELY SCORED BELOW WHAT THE EVIDENCE COUNT SUPPORTS. The rubric makes conviction a count of distinct evidence kinds, and on that count CCJ would be a 5 and the NKE, LULU and LCII long closes would each be a 4. All four are published at 2. This is intentional and recorded by the research phase, not a scoring error: on those rows the evidence runs almost entirely against the position, while the rubric counts confirmations supporting an idea. Publishing a high-conviction BUY for a stock the reader is being told to sell would put a contradiction on the sheet and corrupt the by-conviction performance table. Their key_risk fields each state the thinness, and all four are sized at 0% because they are exits. No score anywhere in this report was raised; the conviction spread is 4x2, 2x3, 3x4, 3x5, which is not the collapse-onto-3 that the record warns about.

SIZE DOES NOT FOLLOW CONVICTION UPWARD TODAY. NKE short and LULU short are conviction 5 but stay at 2% rather than the 4-5% the tier table allows, because both are short equity on margin into a live European credit event and crowded shorts in beaten-up consumer names unwind violently. CEG stays at 3% despite being a 5, because its stop is 1.67 ATR and its forward ratio is 0.41:1. Conviction measures how well evidenced a view is; size measures what the risk can bear, and today those point in different directions.

WHY ONLY ONE NEW IDEA. The tape is an escalating sovereign credit event with the ECB declining to intervene, and 2026-10-07 was indiscriminate de-risking in which gold, miners, uranium, EM and small caps sold together while mega-cap indices barely moved. The bar for fresh long risk went up rather than down. Three setups were researched to completion and rejected on their numbers rather than trimmed to fit: JPM (1.83:1 at the only defensible target, against the 2.0 floor), GS (the ratio passes at 2.71:1 but it is the weakest major name in the weakest sector, -8.2% versus XLF in a month) and a natural gas long (good thesis, but the 200-day sits 2.7% overhead and every passing target is beyond any level that could be pointed at). The idea count is low because the rejections were honest, not because research ran short.

PRICE BASIS — THE PREVIOUS CLOSE, WHICH IS NOT STALE DATA. Every equity and ETF price in this report is the 2026-10-07 16:00 ET regular-session close, refetched at synthesis and unchanged from research (finnhub returns session 'pre', age ~881 minutes). At 06:00 ET that is the freshest honest equity price there is: the market is closed, not the data old. All ten finalist quotes returned ok.

COVERAGE GAPS — EVERY ONE IS A FETCH FAILURE, NOT AN ABSENCE OF SETUPS. No event-contract idea is published because market_data.py events returns count 0 for CPI, recession, FEDDECISION, inflation and unemployment, and for 'Fed' returns six sports markets with every price field null — no implied probability means no honest event idea. No crypto idea is published because spot fetches (BTC $82,733, ETH $2,555.56, SOL $114.50) but history BTC-USD fails on all five sources, so there is no ATR and no support level to set a stop from. No futures idea is published because Robinhood's listing of micro natural gas could not be verified and no live futures price or ATR was fetchable. There is no index, VIX, DXY, gold or crude level this run: Yahoo returned HTTP 429 on both hosts throughout, finnhub refuses indices, stooq 404s on ^ symbols and there is no alphavantage key. THE DOLLAR IS THE GAP THAT MATTERS MOST — EEM is an open long and DXY is its primary driver, so that position is being carried, and halved, without a reading on the thing that moves it. Options-implied moves were unavailable (implied DAL returned HTTP 401), so no target was checked against a straddle; short interest was unavailable (short DAL timed out at api.nasdaq.com). Earnings dates, prices, ATRs, FRED series, insider and analyst data all fetched successfully.

NO INTRADAY IDEAS, AND THAT IS NOT A QUOTA MISS. Horizons are 8 swing and 4 long_term. Nothing intraday cleared the bar, and with equity prices available only as the previous close at 06:00 ET there was no intraday level to set honestly anyway. Nothing was filtered or padded for horizon balance.

SIX UNFILLED ORDERS TO ACT ON, ALL IN THE WATCHLIST. Four cancellations (VST @132.00, GLD @406.77, TLT @79.90, ITB @89.80), one expired event contract to reap (KXFEDDECISION-26SEP-H0 @47), and AAL @13.35 kept live unchanged. None were captured as candidates because a cancellation is not a trade. The VST entry carries the most useful finding of the run: this report correctly identified the hyperscaler-nuclear theme and both names, and the difference in outcome was entry style alone — CEG was entered at the market on 2026-10-01, filled, and is +10.1%, while VST asked for a 132.00 pullback on 2026-08-24, never filled, and the stock has since run +19.1% in two sessions to sit 26.3% above the order. A pullback entry is a bet that you will be given a better price, and on a working thesis you are not.

FOUR OPEN POSITIONS ARE HELD UNCHANGED AND DELIBERATELY NOT RE-EMITTED. XLE (forward 2.79:1, stop 2.12 ATR, all floors clear), KHC (stop is 3.38 ATR from entry and doing its job; hold, do not add, do not widen), PFE (the only open long that rose on 10/07, +1.82%, and closed above its 20- and 50-day) and BCC (hold, do not add, invalidation now stated as the same 5.27% 10-year that closes LCII; if it loses its 90-day low of 67.05 the same reasoning closes it). XLE and PFE have each been recommended three times in the last ten days and nothing changed about either this morning — re-pitching an unchanged idea is the anchoring the duplicate guard exists to prevent, so their absence from the recommendation list is a decision, not an omission.

TWO CORRELATION NOTES. PEP is the second bet on the de-rated packaged-food driver alongside the open KHC long, and is sized and flagged as such in its key_risk. The CEG hold and the CCJ close are the two sides of one theme: the market bought the utility that signed the hyperscaler nuclear contracts and faded the fuel, which is the read-across being priced at zero. No driver carries more than three live ideas.

RED TEAM (phase 2c). Cut nothing to the watchlist and that is the correct outcome, not a rubber stamp: eleven of the twelve rows are instructions on positions that already exist, so demoting one deletes an instruction rather than declining a risk, and the only genuinely new idea — PEP — is gated behind a wait-for-the-print entry that is the most disciplined thing in the report. What the red team did find was a rule this report wrote for itself and then applied to the three positions it liked least.

THE FORWARD-RATIO RULE WAS APPLIED TO THREE OF SIX POSITIONS, AND THE THREE SPARED WERE THE WORST. Synthesis computed the forward ratio for six open positions — CEG 0.41:1, NKE short 0.34:1, DINO 0.69:1, LULU short 0.74:1, SNX 0.86:1, EEM 0.95:1 — named it the reason four rows say trim or halve, then closed SNX and halved DINO and EEM while holding CEG, NKE short and LULU short at full size. Those three are the three worst readings on the list and they are also this report's three conviction-5 rows, which is the author-judging-their-own-idea failure that phase 2c exists for. The stated justification — that the target is nearly here — argues for trimming, not holding: a short remaining move means a small expected gain against an unchanged stop. All three are now halved on the same arithmetic that halved DINO at 0.69:1, which is a worse reading than two of them. No level was moved to achieve this and no target was extended.

CEG IS THE ONE THAT SHOULD HAVE GONE FURTHEST. Its 250.00 stop is 1.67 ATR from entry, the only outright stop_distance failure in the report, and synthesis recorded that widening it to an honest 245.70 cuts reward-to-risk to 1.82:1, under the 2.0 floor. Read the rule the way it is written and the 2.18:1 this position was published on never cleared — it cleared because the stop sat inside the noise. That is the same test SNX was closed in profit for failing, and CEG fails it alongside the worst forward ratio on the book and a catalyst that has already fired (12% re-rating in two sessions, 3.3% from the 90-day high, target 1.55 ATR overhead). Half comes off; the remainder is carried only because the 15-year 2,700 MW tranche is near-term contracted cash flow that has held two sessions without fading. Conviction lowered 5 to 4: its fourth evidence item is filed as counter_argument_answered, but the counter_argument text says "I do not dispute it", so three kinds are load-bearing, not four.

LULU SHORT AUTHORISED AN ADD AT A 0.74:1 FORWARD RATIO. The instruction read "acceptable to carry full size here but not to add above 95" against a 91.88 close, which permits new money below 95 — risking 20.12 to the 112.00 stop to make 14.88, worse than the 0.95:1 that halved EEM in the same report. Permission removed; the row now says do not add at any price. Two further problems are recorded in its counter_argument rather than killed on: the catalyst carrying the trade to 77.00 is Q3 results due late November or early December, outside the 15-session swing horizon, and the target is 7.22 ATR from entry against a 6.0 ATR guide — so the 2.07:1 is measured to a level with no scheduled path inside its own window. Conviction 5 to 4.

THREE SIZE FIELDS CONTRADICTED THEIR OWN INSTRUCTIONS, WHICH IS WHAT A READER SIZES OFF. Checked against state/open_positions.json: DINO is a 3% position shown at 1.5%, which establishes that a trim row halves the field. On that convention CEG was a 2% position shown at 3% under the words DO NOT ADD AT ANY PRICE — the field instructed a 1% add that the text forbids, and the notes above defended it as "CEG stays at 3%"; EEM was a 1% position shown at 1.5% under TRIM HALF, a 50% increase; DAL was a 2% position shown at 1.5% under CUT TO HALF SIZE. Corrected to CEG 1.0 (post-trim), EEM 0.5, DAL 1.0. These are not cosmetic: the size column is the only part of a row that moves money.

TWO CONVICTION SCORES WERE PAID FOR BY ONE CONFIRMATION OR BY NOTHING. DINO 3 to 2 — both evidence items read off the same Nasdaq price series for the same symbol, one filed technical_level and one positioning, which is a single confirmation wearing two kinds and the thing distinct kinds exist to prevent. SNX 4 to 2 — synthesis deliberately scored the CCJ, NKE-long, LULU-long and LCII closes at 2 so that a sell instruction would not reach the sheet as a high-conviction BUY, then missed the fifth close: SNX was a conviction-4 buy whose action is CLOSE AT THE MARKET. It now matches the other four, which keeps the by-conviction table honest.

PEP, THE ONLY NEW IDEA, SURVIVES AND IS SIZED DOWN. 3% to 2%: its own key_risk names it as the second bet on the de-rated packaged-food driver alongside the open KHC long, and a correlation that is named and then sized at the joint-largest in the book has not been acted on. One structural flaw is added to its counter_argument rather than being grounds to cut: the trigger and the void condition are correlated, because the print that takes PEP below 120 is substantially the print that cuts FY2026 EPS guidance below the $8.55 floor and voids the thesis, so this will fail to trigger more often than the three-tranche plan reads. Its missing win_probability was left null against a 27% break-even — inventing one would be fabricating a figure about the report's own idea, which is exactly what this phase does not trust.

A CORRELATION THE REPORT DID NOT NAME. It flags PEP/KHC and the CEG/CCJ two-sided nuclear read-across, and states that no driver carries more than three ideas, but does not identify NKE short and LULU short as one position wearing two tickers: both are de-rated consumer-discretionary brands shorted on repeated guide-downs, same direction, same horizon, both on margin, 4% of the book between them into a live European credit event. Halving both takes the cluster to 2% combined, which is the response the finding calls for; neither is closed outright because both theses are intact and both stops are structurally sound.

NOT ACTED ON, DELIBERATELY. The five close instructions (SNX, CCJ, NKE long, LULU long, LCII) were tested and left alone — each gives the arithmetic for its own exit, each states what would make the exit wrong, and the four that cannot pass a floor say so rather than being trimmed to fit. The repointed Nasdaq source URLs were spot-checked as the human-readable view of the API path research actually fetched, which is a correction and not an invention. The three pre-market spread artifacts (DAL, SNX, LCII) were left at the quoted numbers for the same reason synthesis left them: a bid/ask is not ours to adjust. DAL conviction 4 to 3 is the one remaining downgrade — its positioning evidence is one-month relative strength, which its own counter_argument withdraws as "a bounce inside a downtrend", leaving a dated catalyst and a technical reading whose own content is a close below the 50-day. Half size into a binary print is the right carry; conviction 4 was not paid for.

Net: twelve rows in, twelve rows out, nothing killed. Three positions halved (NKE short, CEG, LULU short), five conviction scores lowered (CEG, LULU short, DAL, DINO, SNX), three size fields corrected to match their own instructions, one add-permission removed, and PEP sized down for a correlation it had already named. Validation demoted 6 idea(s) whose numbers did not check out. 6 more carry warnings — see the validation block on each.

market_context.summary: A live French sovereign-debt scare is the driver of this tape, and it reframes everything else. The 10-year OAT/Bund spread stood at 134.4bp on 2026-10-07 with the OAT at 4.83% against a 3.49% Bund, and one account has it above 150bp on 10/02 — the widest since late 2011. The mechanism is the 2027 draft budget, which needs roughly EUR 54bn of savings to reach a 5% deficit and which investors doubt can be delivered; French bank CDS now price above UK, German, Swiss and Spanish peers, because banks hold the sovereign and the spread marks their books. Stoxx 600 banks fell 3.3% Wednesday and as much as 2.2% on Thursday — the biggest two-day slump since March — with SocGen 25% off its August peak and the CAC 40 at a six-month low of 7,834.10. The Bank of France governor has called the situation serious and explicitly ruled out intervention. US banks were sold in sympathy: JPM 10.1% off its high, GS 23.1%, C 14.0%, WFC 12.8%. The 2026-10-07 US session was not a broad decline but a targeted de-risking of the commodity and reflation trade: SPY -0.24% and QQQ -0.25% essentially flat while IWM fell 1.29%, GDX 3.13%, CCJ 4.25% and EEM 1.32%. The detail that should make anyone cautious is that gold fell too — GLD -1.67% on a day of sovereign credit fear is not a flight to safety, it is positions being reduced for liquidity, and that is the regime in which buying dips has the worst odds. Underneath, the rate configuration is stagflationary: fed funds 3.88% against a 5.27% 10-year, the 10y-2y curve steepening to +0.51 from +0.48 (term premium being added), unemployment up to 4.2% from 4.1%, and August CPI +0.40% m/m. That mix is hostile to long-duration equity and to rate-sensitive discretionary names, which is where this report's open book has been concentrated. Consequence for today: the bar for new long risk went up, not down. One new idea is published. Note on the levels below: they are the 2026-10-07 closes, and SPY/QQQ/IWM/XLF/XLE/GLD/TLT stand in for index, VIX, DXY, gold and crude levels, which could not be fetched at all this run — Yahoo returned HTTP 429 throughout. The missing dollar reading is the one that matters, because EEM is an open long.

recommendations.thesis: This is an update to an open NKE short, not a new idea. The thesis is the guide, not the chart: on 2026-10-01 Nike reported Q1 FY2027 revenue down 4% to $11.21bn against ~$11.35bn expected and guided FY2027 adjusted EPS to $1.15-1.35 against a ~$1.69 consensus, a cut of roughly 30% to the year the market was underwriting, with Greater China down 26% currency-neutral. Price has confirmed rather than led: the close of 34.36 is below both the 20-day at 35.70 and the 50-day at 38.47. The reason to hold rather than add is that the target is nearly here.
recommendations.key_risk: A short carried into a restructuring story is the wrong side of any credible self-help news. Nike has announced Pace, targeting about $2.5bn of savings by end-FY2031, and a single buyback, China stabilisation datapoint or activist headline squeezes a crowded, heavily-owned mega-cap hard. The position requires margin, so the 41.00 stop is 19.3% above the current close and a gap can cost more than the 2.60 nominally risked per share.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against is valuation: at 34.36 NKE is near its 90-day low of 31.97 and 25.8% off the high, so the bad guide is substantially in the price, and shorting a trough multiple on a brand of this quality has a poor history. That is precisely why the instruction is trim-at-target rather than press — the remaining 2.26 of downside to 32.10 against 6.64 of stop distance is no longer an attractive risk, and the honest action on a short that has worked is to take it off, not to re-argue it.

recommendations.thesis: A mega-cap staple has been de-rated 28% to a one-year low of 123.47 while its own earnings guidance held: management has reiterated FY2026 EPS of $8.55-8.71, which puts the 123.73 close at roughly 14.3x the midpoint against the low-20s multiple PEP has historically carried. The problem causing the de-rating is specific and locatable rather than diffuse — Frito-Lay North America volume went flat despite price cuts of up to 15% on Lay's and Doritos, PepsiCo Beverages North America volume fell 4% (the steepest since Q2 2020), and core operating margin contracted 40bps in Q2 — while the international segments posted solid gains. That is the shape of a fixable regional execution problem priced as a terminal one, which is what the long_term lane is for. The multiple compressed; the earnings did not.
recommendations.key_risk: The specific risk is that the volume decline is not a pricing problem at all. PEP already cut prices up to 15% and volume did not respond, which says the issue may be demand for the category rather than its cost — GLP-1 adoption and a durable shift away from salty snacks and sugared drinks would make 14.3x the new fair multiple rather than a discount, and the earnings base would then follow volume down. Sentiment confirms the risk rather than the opportunity: analyst bullish share is only 40.0% and fell 4.8 points over four months (strong buys 3 to 2, holds 15 to 17), JPMorgan cut to Neutral from Overweight and Deutsche Bank to Hold from Buy, both citing North America, and there has been no open-market insider buying in six months. Note also the correlation: KHC is already an open staples long in this book, so this is the second bet on the same de-rated-packaged-food driver and should be sized as such.
